question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, notice that:

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $x$-axis. Since ${e}^{t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $y$-axis. Since ${e}^{2t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$

Among the given options, there are two phase portraits satisfying these conditions:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14147756/assets/a2c81ff3c50013c149dc6a5db67bbe11cccdbbef22ce2c0712101f4a358bcb8c.png)

Let's consider the solutions $x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{t}$ and $y(t)={c}_{2}{e}^{2t}$ provided that ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\ne 0.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}=\frac{({c}_{2}{e}^{2t})^{′}}{({c}_{1}{e}^{t})^{′}}=\frac{2{c}_{2}{e}^{2t}}{{c}_{1}{e}^{t}}=\frac{2{c}_{2}}{{c}_{1}}{e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\to \pm \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ meaning that the tangents to the solution become more and more vertical as we move away from the origin. This corresponds to the following phase portrait:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14147756/assets/9ab329eed7e67e017a822e8d5163b331e0c93a9747f74aee3a10d6592f44a59b.png)
